newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore telecom show attracts world players.
newsitem.headline: Singapore telecom show attracts world players.

text.p: Hundreds of the world's big electronics and telecommunications companies gathered in Singapore on Sunday ahead of an exhibition showcasing the city state's effort to become an information-communication hub.
Asia Telecom 97, the fourth international telecom exhibition for the Asia-Pacific region, formally kicks off on Monday and runs until June 14.
The exhibition is organised by the International Telecommunication Union, a U.N. body which sets international technical standards on communication, every four years.

Deregulation in the telecommunications sector in many Asian countries has boosted the number of new operators and opened markets in the region, and telecommunications carriers and electronics manufacturers have rushed to set up joint ventures and seek operation partners in the region.
More than 350 exhibitors from 25 countries will show their latest technologies. Many governments have also rented stands since state ownership is still common in the industry.

During the show, Singapore will launch aspects of its "Singapore One" multimedia project, which aims to connect every home in the country to multi-media services on a high-speed, large-capacity fibre-optics network.
Malaysia and other Asian nations will also be touting their potential for high-tech industry and investment and for next- generation info-computer systems this week.
American and Japanese phone operators are showing their next-generation phone systems in a bid to make their own technologies an international standard.

Despite a large potential, a wide diversity in teledensity -- the number of phones installed among the population -- is one of the biggest problems of the Asian region, ITU said. There are also wide differences in services available.

The ITU said telephone networks in the emerging markets of the Asia-Pacific grew at an annual rate of 27 percent in the first half of the 1990s. In China and some other countries, annual network growth is now over 40 percent.
Telecommunication investments throughout most of the countries of the Asia-Pacific region are estimated at US$1.5 to two trillion over the next 10 years.
But despite the efforts thus far, as many as two thirds of Asia's people do not have even ready access to a simple telephone.

Pekka Tarjanne, Secretary General of the ITU, told a news conference on Sunday: "We must not exacerbate the gap that already exists between the developed and the developing world, or create a divided society of 'information haves' and 'information have-nots'."

Under the theme "Asian routes towards the Global Information Society," the participants at Asia Telecom will discuss technical and financing schemes and deregulation needed to transform high-growth potential into reality.
